      SDRF indicative claim

      Norms: Rs 5,000 per pole, Rs 0.50 lakh per km, Rs 1.0 lakh per DTR. LT AB cable may not qualify as bare-conductor line.

      Building back resilient (CEA Task Force)

      • Double-pole structure with AB switch every 10 poles – first on SKP HQ, Pallipalem, Mori, KD Palem, Gondi Industrial.
      • Spun / rail poles and intermediate poles on rebuilt spans.
      • Plinth-mounted 3-Ph DTRs – Gondi Industrial (31 DTRs); stronger 1-Ph structures – Rameswaram (8).
      • AB cable for LT near the sea – Antarvedi, Appanaramuni Lanka.
      • RCC / pre-cast foundations in paddy and aqua bunds; epoxy coating against salt corrosion.
      • GPS mapping of every DTR and pole; split long feeders (KD Palem 17 km).
      • Permanent 50-person restoration shelter at each 33/11 KV SS; 250-person village shelters.

      Feedback and reporting system

      One format, two reporting times, one owner per line
      • 10:00 AM and 4:00 PM – each officer-in-charge reports feeder, team, poles erected, spans strung, DTRs charged, services restored, labour, machinery, material short and help needed.
      • Control room consolidates feeder-wise and SS-wise status in the cyclone data format the same hour; follows up a missing report within 30 minutes.
      • 8:00 PM – Mandal review with the MRO; Overall In-charge sends the mandal report to Division and Circle (BRK Circle Arnab format: SS / feeders pending, villages, damages, dumping, batches, labour, officer, crane and PDM).
      • Village level – village secretary and volunteers report unrestored houses by WhatsApp; complaint register logs each with time closed.
      • Evidence – GPS-stamped before/after photos for every pole location and DTR, kept feeder-wise.
      • WhatsApp group per SS and one mandal group carry the reports.

      PROJECT

      PUNARJYOTHI

      Restore · Rebuild · Resilient

      A ready-to-use disaster-management framework for power distribution networks hit by cyclones, floods and storms – from the first IMD warning to the last service restored. Use it for any district, circle or mandal: the norms, checklists, calculators and 20 Excel templates work as they are.

        Material chain

        Damage enumeration→Requirement (area / DTR-wise)→Indent→Receipt at sub-store→Issue to batch→Utilisation at pole / DTR→Balance → next indent

        Every step is one line in a register (templates 03–08, 20). Unused material is devolved back and accounted item-wise after the restoration.

        Pole types – specification and handling

        Source: AP common Standard Schedule of Rates, 2021-22. Prefer spun poles on rebuilt spans of the worst-hit feeders.

        Pre-stock list for each sub-store

        Procurement rules

        • Split pole orders type-wise across several approved manufacturers; no single factory sets the pace.
        • Ask each manufacturer for a daily dispatch quantity and the nearest delivery point.
        • Record ordered, dispatched, received and balance daily; late orders turn red.
        • Plan lorries and cranes from weight, not count.
        • Keep Annual Rate Contracts in coastal areas so material and workforce come without tender delay.
        • Record spares on the DRIPS portal; review the material bank before every cyclone season.
        • After restoration, devolve unused material and arrive at quantities material-wise.

        CPM / PERT – one feeder

        Critical path A → B → E → F → G → J → K = 10.5 days. Protect material dumping (B).

        Daily rhythm

        Reporting system

        • 10 AM and 4 PM – officer-in-charge reports: poles, spans, DTRs, services, labour, machinery, material short, help needed (template 14).
        • Same hour – control room consolidates feeder-wise and SS-wise; chases a missing report within 30 minutes.
        • 8 PM – review chaired with the revenue authority; next day's plan and machinery moves.
        • Village level – unrestored houses reported by volunteers; complaint register logs time closed.
        • Evidence – GPS-stamped before/after photo for every pole and DTR.
        • Micro – span-by-span on the feeder sketch. Macro – % of km per feeder across the area.

        Bottlenecks and corrections

        Assurance of electrification

        Service list DTR-wise from billing→House-to-house tick by lineman + volunteer→Unrestored list to officer the same evening→Certificate signed by AE, Village Secretary, VRO→Village closed in daily report

        Camp norms

        Payments – no cash in the field

        Permanent restoration shelter – 50 persons at each 33/11 KV SS

        Plinth about 420–430 m²; plinth above highest flood level; RCC frame for the coastal wind zone; RO plant, 5,000 L tank, generator + rooftop solar.

        Village multi-purpose shelter – 250 persons

        Every shelter needs a management committee, a maintenance fund and a peace-time use from day one.
